title: Bench results
description: Every computed number for one run set, produced by `python -m bench.metrics score` from committed manifests and run envelopes and nothing else. The README results table (bench/report.py) is generated from this file and only this file: no number appears in any document in this repository that is not present here. This file is results version 1.1.0 and validates 1.x documents only.
$comment: Results version 1.1.0. `entries[]` holds one row per (skill, skill_version, model, domain) group, baseline rows included: a baseline run carries skill "baseline-generic" in the same array, at the same shape, so a report script computes a skill-versus-baseline comparison by matching (domain, model) pairs rather than reading a separately stored, and therefore possibly stale, comparison table. 1.1.0 added recall_location and precision_location (P3 rescore, bench/results/README.md, "Baseline comparison"): recall.value and precision.value require an exact criterion-string match between a finding and a planted defect, which pins baseline-generic at exactly 0.0 everywhere because every baseline finding carries the fixed criterion BASELINE-GENERIC that no manifest plants a defect under; recall_location and precision_location apply the same per-artifact-type location tolerance with the criterion check dropped, so a skill and the baseline can be compared on whether either one pointed at the right place at all. Additive and backward-compatible: every 1.0.0 field keeps its old meaning and value.

run_set.title: Run set identifier
run_set.description: Matches the directory name under bench/results/ this file lives in, for example bench/results/p3-2026-08-01/results.json has run_set "p3-2026-08-01".

generated_at.description: When `python -m bench.metrics score` produced this file.

entries.title: Scored entries
entries.description: One entry per (skill, skill_version, model, domain) group actually present in --runs. Empty is valid: a run set with no matched envelopes produces an empty array rather than an error, so an incomplete run set is still a well-formed file.

skill.title: Skill name
skill.description: The emitting skill, matching the contract's run.skill: "critique-clarity", or "baseline-generic" for the frozen baseline comparison.

model.title: Model ID
model.description: Exact pinned model identifier, matching the contract's run.model. Benchmark numbers are only honest if this is pinned.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The bench domain scored, matching manifest.schema.json's domain field.

artifact_type.title: Artifact type
artifact_type.description: The location-tolerance rule this domain's artifacts use, matching manifest.schema.json's artifactType.

artifacts_scored.title: Artifacts scored
artifacts_scored.description: How many (manifest, envelope) pairs contributed to this entry's recall, precision, and clean_fp_rate. Not necessarily the corpus's full artifact count for this domain: an entry only reflects the envelopes actually present under --runs.

unresolvable_claims.title: Unresolvable claims
unresolvable_claims.description: Count of claims whose location resolved to no anchor at all, summed across every scored artifact in this entry. Reported per S-03 OQ-1's RC review question: whether the resolver's parse failures are common enough to distort the numbers. An unresolvable claim is still a miss for recall and still counts against precision; this field does not change either computation, it only makes the size of that approximation visible.

recall.description: Criterion-level recall: matched planted defects, over planted defects, where a match requires exact criterion-string equality plus a location within the artifact type's tolerance (bench/README.md, "Recall"). Primary for a skill: it measures rubric operationalization, whether the skill named the defect under the criterion the rubric assigns it, not only whether it noticed something at the right place. Pinned at 0.0 for baseline-generic by construction; see recall_location for the comparison that is not.

precision.description: Criterion-level precision: claims matched to a planted defect under the same criterion-plus-location predicate as recall, over all claims emitted (bench/README.md, "Precision"). Pinned at 0.0 for baseline-generic by construction; see precision_location.

recall_location.description: Location-level recall: matched planted defects, over planted defects, where a match requires only a location within the artifact type's tolerance, criterion ID ignored entirely (bench/metrics/score.py, score_artifact_location). Computed from the same envelopes as recall, no new runs. This is the fair cross-condition figure: baseline-generic findings carry no rubric criterion, so criterion-level recall could not have been anything but 0.0 no matter what the model wrote, and recall_location is the number that is not pinned by that construction.

precision_location.description: Location-level precision: claims matched to a planted defect by location alone, criterion ID ignored, over all claims emitted (bench/metrics/score.py, score_artifact_location). Computed from the same envelopes as precision, no new runs. Read beside precision the same way recall_location is read beside recall.

clean_fp_rate.description: Mean claims per clean artifact (bench/README.md, "False positives on clean artifacts"). Reported separately from precision because it isolates the behavior that matters most to a user: what the skill says about a document with nothing wrong with it.

consistency.description: Mean pairwise Jaccard, tolerance-aware, over k runs of the same skill against the same artifact, averaged with equal weight across every scored artifact that had at least two runs to compare.

consistency_exact.description: The same aggregation as consistency, computed with zero tolerance on the canonical (criterion, key) sets. The gap between consistency and consistency_exact is the skill's location-phrasing instability.

metricValue.title: A ratio, plus the integers it was formed from
metricValue.description: value is null when denominator is 0: the metric is not computable from what was scored, a different claim from "scored and found to be zero". Value, when not null, is rounded to three decimal places (bench/README.md, "Metrics": "a ratio is formed once, at the end, and reported to three decimal places"); numerator and denominator are the exact integers the ratio was formed from, so the rounding is always auditable.

consistencyValue.title: A consistency figure, plus how many artifacts and pairs it was formed from
consistencyValue.description: Aggregated with equal weight across every scored artifact that had at least two runs to compare (see bench/metrics/score.py's module docstring for why this module, not bench/README.md, fixes that convention). value is null when no artifact in this entry had two or more runs.

artifacts_with_pairs.title: Artifacts with pairs
artifacts_with_pairs.description: How many artifacts contributed a computable per-artifact consistency value to this entry's mean.

total_pairs.title: Total pairs
total_pairs.description: Sum, across every contributing artifact, of the C(k, 2) unordered run pairs compared.

resultsVersion.title: Results version
resultsVersion.description: Version of this results format, versioned independently of both the plugin and the critique contract. This file validates 1.x results documents only.

semver.title: Semantic version
semver.description: Copied verbatim from the critique contract's semver. Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, with no leading v.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Copied verbatim from the critique contract's timestamp. RFC 3339 in UTC with a literal trailing Z, optional fractional seconds.
